hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions on the real product: every action is denied unless a role grants it
hard_gates.evidence: Product fault at 5e80b6c3. This commit carries p12-jobs r2's code (68ffe4ba is an ancestor). It does not carry that piece's fix (4f319b38 and 75f69351 are not ancestors). On my demo (attack/schedule-planner.mjs, output in attack/schedule-planner.txt) the alnoor admin made a role with only jobs.schedules.create and jobs.schedules.read, and a user holding it. As that user: POST /api/jobs/jobs {type:'jobs.cleanup'} -> 403 and GET /api/jobs/jobs -> 403. But POST /api/jobs/schedules {type:'jobs.cleanup', cron:'* * * * *', payload:{retentionDays:30}, isEnabled:true} -> 201. Within a minute the scheduler ran job 01a19b17-0b30-722d-8a34-0d86157ada57 (source 'scheduler', status succeeded, result deleted:9), and the job total went from 50,000 to 49,992. ScheduleEndpoints.Create checks only that the kind is schedulable, never the kind's run permission. A user without a kind's run permission can therefore run it as system work.

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's live attack as tenant A (alnoor) against tenant B (gulfsteel)
hard_gates.evidence: attack/attack.mjs is round 15's script with jobs and schedules added (B's job and schedule ids in every route, job lists in filters, job exports) and a jobs body (type, cron, payload naming B's tenant). It made 191 operations with B ids, 1,210 documented query-parameter requests (cookie and bearer), 810 tenant-switch header, query and cookie requests, 150 export requests (10 lists, csv/xlsx/pdf/json/html, en/ar) and 63 filter, search and cursor requests. No B marker or B-only id appeared (550 B ids collected, 0 shared with A). The md5 checksum of every tenant table's rows for B was unchanged after the attack and again later (attack/b-before-attack.txt, b-now.txt). The single flagged line is DELETE /api/currency/rates/{B id} -> 204 with B's row unchanged, which round 15 also noted (the same answer as for a missing id). A's clean-up job with payload tenantId=B deleted 50,001 of A's own jobs and none of B's 1,000 (db-jobs-after-attack.txt).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the database role the app uses
hard_gates.evidence: db-roles-rls.txt: erp_app, erp_auth and erp_owner are all not superuser and have no BYPASSRLS; postgres is the only superuser. erp_owner owns all 34 tables. All 25 tenant_id columns are NOT NULL. Every table with tenant_id has RLS enabled and forced and a tenant_isolation policy (tenant_id = erp.current_tenant_id()). The policies whose USING is true are limited to erp_auth (auth resolver, due-tenants lookup), or are RESTRICTIVE company write policies. The app container connects as erp_app.

hard_gates.gate: G1 gate self-check: a tenant leak planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L16 (plants/plants.diff) is a middleware in UseErpPlatform, after UseAuthorization. It keeps the users list's search answers for 120 s in a DI singleton (CriticWarmAnswers, a ConcurrentDictionary keyed by path and query, no tenant). It is live: CriticR16Proof shows A's search returning B's rows (plant-PROOFALL.log). It was caught statically (plant-G1STATIC.log): G1ProcessStateTests flagged 'singleton Erp.Kernel.Hosting.CriticWarmAnswers._answers ... mutable ConcurrentDictionary', and G1TenantSourceTests flagged ErpPlatform.cs:226 for request enumeration.

hard_gates.gate: G2 gate self-check: an unchecked action planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant P16 is in PermissionAuthorizationHandler (src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Security/Permissions.cs). It lets any signed-in request through when the path does not start with '/api/', using an ordinal, case-sensitive test. ASP.NET routing ignores case, so /API/identity/users reaches the users endpoint. It is live (plant-PROOFALL.log): a no-roles user gets 403 on /api/identity/users and 200 on /API/identity/users and /Api/Identity/Roles. All 159 G2, Rules and SelfTests tests passed with the plant (plant-G2P16.log, 46.2 min), and so did the static G2ClientAddressCodeTests. On the real product, the unplanted control (plant-PROOFNONE.log) gives 403 on every letter case, so this is a gate gap, not a product fault.

biggest_gap.title: At this commit a user who may only add schedules can run job kinds they are refused, and p00's G2 gate machinery does not catch it
biggest_gap.detail: The judged commit 5e80b6c3 contains p12-jobs round 2's schedules code without its later fix. POST /api/jobs/schedules (ScheduleEndpoints.Create) checks jobs.schedules.create and that the kind is schedulable. It never checks the kind's own run permission. The scheduler then queues the job as system work with source 'scheduler' and no requesting user. So jobs.schedules.create is in effect permission to run every schedulable kind. Today that includes the clean-up that deletes job history. Later it will include whatever schedulable work other modules add: payroll runs, period closing, bulk postings, all of which a UAE trading or manufacturing company guards with their own permissions. It is a real missing permission check, so the round is BLOCKED whichever piece wrote the handler. It is also p00's gap: the shared G2 gate checks that one permission opens exactly the endpoints that declare it. It does not check that what an endpoint sets in motion stays within the caller's grants. The fix for this case is on the integration branch (4f319b38 'schedules added switched off need only jobs.schedules.create', 75f69351 'G2 subject gate', merged at 72fa2f65), so a re-judgement at a commit that contains it should clear the product fault. The gate-side weakness also shows in my plant P16 (see gate_gaps): G2 still varies only the client address. It does not vary the Host (backlog row 3, still open) or the letter case of the path.
biggest_gap.evidence: To reproduce on a demo of 5e80b6c3: run attack/schedule-planner.mjs (BASE=http://localhost:<port>). It signs in as admin@alnoor.example, makes a role ['jobs.schedules.create','jobs.schedules.read'] and a user with it, then acts as that user. Output (attack/schedule-planner.txt): POST /api/jobs/jobs {type:'jobs.cleanup'} -> 403, GET /api/jobs/jobs -> 403, POST /api/jobs/schedules {scheduleName, type:'jobs.cleanup', cron:'* * * * *', payload:{retentionDays:30}, isEnabled:true} -> 201. Then 'schedule ran job 01a19b17-...', and the admin view shows status succeeded, source scheduler, result {deleted:9}; the admin's job total went from 50,000 to 49,992. To confirm the commit has no fix: git merge-base --is-ancestor 4f319b38 5e80b6c3 returns false. Source: src/Modules/Jobs/Erp.Modules.Jobs/Schedules/ScheduleEndpoints.cs line 195, validator.Must(type is { Schedulable: true }, ...), with no RunPermission check.

other_findings: [route: p12-jobs] The job worker container is given the owner role's connection string (ConnectionStrings__Owner, user erp_owner, the owner of all 34 tables). JobRunner.DueTenantsAsync uses it to SET LOCAL ROLE erp_auth. erp_owner has no BYPASSRLS and RLS is forced, so I found no leak. But a process that runs every module's job handlers holds credentials that can ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY or drop a policy. p00's spec says the application connects as a role that is neither superuser nor table owner. A login role that is only a member of erp_auth would avoid this. Seen with docker exec <worker> printenv (db-roles-rls.txt lists the roles).

[route: p01-odoo-rig] The only failing stage of my verify was the e2e ours-drivers health check. add-rate and create-company-branch were invalid with 'the page changed what it shows without a counted step causing it ... a page task no step caused'. The load was 20 to 35 on 16 threads at 12:45-12:51Z, and all 18 other suite results passed. This is the same failure class p12 r2's critic saw under load in serial-14. I did not re-run the full verify, because the round is BLOCKED on the product fault anyway and the slot queue had taken 4 hours. Under the rule, a round still needs one full passing verify.

Running build/ratchet-check.mjs by hand on the failed folder reports suite.dotnetTests 892 < minimum 900 (ratchet-check.txt). The likely cause is that the timing stage (Load=Timing tests, including the new RequestCostTests ceiling run alone) was skipped once e2e failed, so this is probably not a lost test. An integrator's passing run should confirm that 900 is reached.

Processor time 11,489 s (dotnet 8,437.5, web 2,389.0, e2e 662.2) against the 10,600 s maximum, on a busy machine: load was 46 to 74 when the slot was taken, and my plant run used the toolbox for 50 min beside it. G1HttpIsolationTests.Tenant_A_cannot_reach_tenant_B_through_any_endpoint alone took 1 h 29 m wall and kept the dotnet stage to a single busy core for its last ~90 min. The integrator's alone run is the measure (#22, #31).

Gate backlog row 3 (G2 never varies the Host header, plant P13 from r14) is still open. This round's gate code does not vary the request beyond the client address. On the real product no Host or letter-case variant opened anything for a no-roles user.
